ornaments: woodcut headpiece band above the title (grotesques, foliage, central urn)
decorated initial A, 5 lines, white-on-black foliate block, opening AV MOIS
typographic fleuron printed before the italic heading Texte de la Toile du procés,

uncertain.note: the folio glyph is a serifed vertical stroke that looks like a roman I; read as the arabic figure 1 because the same shape is used twice for folio 11 on p011 and the book foliates in arabic figures (p002 = 2)
a small round dot sits on the baseline immediately after DV; it is lighter and smaller than the page's printed points, so it may be a printed full stop (DV.) or an ink speck. Transcribed without it.
both e's of 'memorable' print with almost no crossbar, so the word reads as 'mcmorablc' on the sheet; read as 'memorable' from sense and from the same weak e elsewhere on the page

the mark over the e of 'cẽt' is broad, horizontal and wavy (a tilde: cẽt = cent, i.e. cent & onze annotations), clearly unlike the short steep acute of 'procés' on the next-but-one line; a reader could take it for 'cét'

a faint thin caret/tilde-shaped mark is printed over the o of 'tations'; it is much lighter than the surrounding type and the n is set in full, so it looks accidental (rising quad or offset) rather than a nasal abbreviation. Transcribed as a plain o.

uncertain.text: pour lors auſsi fort ieune, & preſque de
uncertain.note: 'auſsi' is set with a long s followed by a round s (not ſſ); transcribed as printed per §2

a single 'A' stands alone below the last body line, right of centre rather than at the usual left/centre signature position; read as the gathering signature and not a catchword, because p002 opens with the heading ANNOTATION I. and the word 'Les'
MOIS is set with light letterspacing between its capitals, much narrower than the wide spacing of A R R E S T; treated as an ordinary word, not as spaced capitals
